intent: Divide two runs of an InputOtp's slots with a muted glyph.
typical_uses: The divider between the two halves of a split code

dont_use_when.situation: A divider between content anywhere outside an InputOtp

invariants.text: With no children the separator renders a dash inside a span marked `aria-hidden="true"`; children, when given, replace that span and are rendered as they are, with no `aria-hidden` added.
`orientation` sets the stamped `aria-orientation` and `data-orientation` and nothing else: input-otp.module.css has no orientation selector, so the separator looks the same either way.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the separator inside an InputOtpGroup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place it directly inside the InputOtp root, between two groups

a11y.by: The primitive's Separator (role="separator" with aria-orientation) plus input-otp.test.tsx's assertion that the rendered field contains an element with role separator

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input-otp.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The default dash between two groups
A custom glyph in place of the dash

bad.title: A separator with no InputOtp around it
bad.why: InputOtpSeparator exists to divide slot groups inside an InputOtp and draws a muted glyph; a general content divider is the kit's Separator, which draws a line.
